newsitem.title: CHINA: Shun Shing changes name to COSCO Int'l.
newsitem.headline: Shun Shing changes name to COSCO Int'l.

text.p: Shareholders of Shun Shing Holdings Ltd gave the green light on Wednesday to a change in the company name to COSCO International Holdings Ltd.
They also approved an increase in the number of directors and in authorised share capital.

"The name change primarily reflects the change in control of the management of the company and reinforces the fact that the company, similar to COSCO Pacific Ltd, is one of the listed flagships of COSCO (H.K.) Group Ltd," said vice chairman Zhang Dachun after the company general meeting on Wednesday.

"The company will focus its efforts on property development, infrastructure and construction," said Zhang, who is also the vice chairman of COSCO Pacific. "We will streamline non-profitable projects," he said.

The maximum number of directors of the company has been increased to 20 from 12, aiming to facilitate the anticipated significant enlargement of the company's business portfolio and scale of operations, the company said in a statement.
The authorised share capital of the company has been increased to HK$300 million from HK$100 million by creating an additional two billion shares, it said.

The enlarged capital base will supply sufficient funds for financing future expansion, including investment in roads, bridges, property development, construction and infrastructure in Hong Kong and China, and the South East Asia Region, it said.
In February, COSCO (H.K.) had made a general offer for Shun Shing shares after it raised its stake in the company to a controlling 61 percent from 30 percent.

"As there is an undertaking of not injecting or disposing any company assets before September 27, the proposed assets injection by parent COSCO (H.K.) is likely to take place later after that date and will be in accordance with asset injection guidelines on red-chips," said executive director Kelvin Wong.
Wong said most of the assets to be injected had been held by the parent for more than three years but he declined to comment on the value and the financing methods of the asset purchase.

In June, the company said it was considering buying assets from parent COSCO (H.K.), including office, residential property and hotel redevelopment projects in Hong Kong and in Guangzhou, Shanghai, Beijing and Tianjin in China.
The company had also said it would buy from the parent a coal-fire power plant in Henan, a toll highway in Yunnan, a hydro-electric power plant in Jianngxi and a toll bridge in Guangdong.
It said it would also buy into certain locally listed companies involved in hotel operation and management, property development and toll road operation in China.
COSCO (H.K.) is an arm of China's state-owned China Ocean Shipping (Group) Co.
